title: Brined Panko Chicken Parmesan with Gochujang-Guanciale Tomato Sauce
summary: Thin, brined chicken breast cutlets coated in seasoned flour, egg and panko, shallow-fried until crisp, then broiled under a tomato sauce deepened with gochujang and crisp guanciale and a blend of two mozzarellas and pecorino.
notes: Video: 'The Best Chicken Parmesan Ever' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish (it embeds this video): https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-perfect-cheesy-chicken-parmesan-recipe (serves 4, hands-on prep 30 min, cook 40 min; brining 3-4 hours or overnight is extra and not in prep_minutes). The video gives no serving count, so servings and times come from the written recipe. The video states the chicken, the brine, the sauce, the breading and the cheeses. Where the two differ, the video wins: the flour is seasoned with the 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper (the page puts them in the eggs), the sauce reduces about 5 minutes (page: 15-20) and the oil is about 1/2 inch deep (page: about 1 inch). From the written recipe: panko 2 cups (video: two to three cups), large eggs, kosher salt for the flour. Ranges: water to rinse the tomato can, 1/4-1/2 cup (we use 1/4 cup; it reduces off and has no calories). Our estimates: 1/2 tsp kosher salt to season the sauce (house rule: small estimated salt is counted), a pinch of sugar read as 0.3 g. House rules applied: the brine (water, salt, lemon, garlic, chili flakes, peppercorns, rosemary) is poured off and the chicken rinsed, so none of it is counted, and sodium the meat takes up is not captured. Flour, salt, pepper and panko are dredge, counted at 25%; the egg wash (eggs and water) is counted at 50%. The 1/2-inch oil in a 12-inch skillet is treated as frying oil (it does not stay with the food): it is excluded and 112 g absorbed oil is added (10% of the coated raw weight, arithmetic on that line). The rosemary sprig fried in the oil and the thyme bundle in the sauce are removed. The whole batch of sauce goes on the chicken (he says there is just enough), so it is counted. All the cheese is counted, though he says there is more than enough, so cheese may be somewhat overstated. Not counted (house rule 11, optional and not added in the video): black pepper in the sauce, and the chives and extra pecorino garnish. Named alternatives not counted: bacon for the guanciale. Proxies: guanciale uses USDA fresh pork jowl (sodium understated); red pepper flakes use USDA ground red pepper; panko uses USDA plain dry breadcrumbs, which weigh more per cup than panko.

steps.text: Trim any excess fat from the chicken breasts, then slice each one horizontally all the way through into two thinner pieces.
Between two sheets of plastic wrap or parchment, pound each piece to an even thickness of about 1/3 inch.
Brine: whisk the kosher salt into the water until dissolved. Add the sliced lemon, garlic, red pepper flakes, peppercorns and the rosemary sprigs, crushed in your hand to release their oils.
Lay the cutlets into the brine one at a time so liquid sits between them, make sure all are submerged, cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 3-4 hours).

Sauce: cut the guanciale into 1/4-inch cubes. In a medium saucepan over medium to medium-low heat, coat it in the olive oil and render 2-4 minutes, stirring now and then, then raise to medium and cook 2-3 minutes more until deep brown and crisp.
Lift the guanciale out with a slotted spoon onto paper towels, leaving the fat in the pot. Let it cool, then chop it very finely or pulse it in a blender (not to a paste).
Over medium heat, cook the sliced garlic in the fat just until fragrant, about 15-20 seconds, without browning. Stir in the gochujang and fry it 1-2 minutes until it darkens a little.

Add the sugar, a little salt and the red pepper flakes, then the crushed tomatoes, rinsing the can with the water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, add the thyme bundle and reduce about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it clings to a spoon.
Remove the thyme, stir in the chopped guanciale, and adjust the salt (and pepper, if you like).
Heat about 1/2 inch of high-heat oil in a 12-inch deep cast-iron skillet over medium heat to about 350°F.
Set up three stations: flour seasoned with the salt and pepper; the eggs whisked smooth with the water; and the panko.

Drain the brined chicken, rinse it briefly so it is not too salty, then coat each cutlet in seasoned flour (shake off the excess), then egg, then panko, pressing so there are no bare spots. Set on a sheet tray.

Lay a cutlet into the oil away from you and keep the pan gently moving. Once it starts to color, add a rosemary sprig. Fry 2-3 minutes, flip, and fry 2-3 minutes more, until golden and 165°F inside. Drain on a wire rack; remove the rosemary. Repeat with the rest.
Toss the two mozzarellas and the pecorino together.
Move the cutlets to a foil-lined baking sheet. Spread about 4 oz of sauce on each, keeping it on the chicken, then mound the cheese on top and press it down lightly.
Broil on high 4-6 minutes, checking at 3-4 minutes, until the cheese is melted with some browning. Serve as is or with chives or more pecorino.
